fields.meta_title: Password Reset Form Builder for IT Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a password reset form that names the locked account, sends each request to IT, and never asks for a password. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Password Reset Form That Never Asks for a Password
fields.hero_description: Build a password reset form that sends each lockout to IT with the account named and no password typed in.
fields.features_heading: What IT Needs Before It Resets Anything
fields.features_subheading: Describe who gets locked out and which accounts they use. Emergent builds the form, the queue IT works from, and the alerts.
fields.feature_1:
No field for the old or new password

The form asks for a name, work email, employee ID, the locked account, and what happened. No password passes through it, and none ever sits in the request table IT reads.
fields.feature_2:
Requests that go to the account's owner

Pick Email and the request lands in the help desk queue. Pick Payroll and it goes to whoever runs payroll access, with the employee ID and work email already filled in.
fields.feature_3:
A callback before anyone resets it

The request record carries a Verified box the tech ticks after calling the number on file. The app will not mark a reset done until that box holds a check and the tech's name.
fields.feature_4:
Urgent when the account may be misused

Answer that another person may have signed in, and the request is marked Urgent. The security lead gets a Slack message naming the account and the time it was filed.
fields.feature_5:
Repeat lockouts, counted per person

A dashboard counts requests by account and by month. Anyone with 3 or more resets in 30 days lands on a short list, with the date of each reset and the account it was for.
fields.feature_6:
Your GitHub repository holds the code

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run the form beside your current help desk. The request table and the routing rules move with it.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Is Locked Out, and Who Resets It
fields.tab_content_1:
Back into email 14 minutes after the lockout

Ferelith Ainscough at Kittiwake Accounting is locked out of email at 8:52 am. She files from her phone with her employee ID and "Forgot password." Tech Cosmo Lightbody calls her desk extension from the staff directory, not a number typed into the form. He resets the account at 9:06 am.
fields.tab_content_2:
If someone else used it, the security lead hears first

Leasing agent Peregrine Gorringe at Lowestoft Residential sees a payroll sign-in he never made. He picks Payroll and "Someone else may have used it." That answer marks the request Urgent and sends security lead Ondine Cobbold a Slack message. It stays at the top of the help desk queue until she closes it.
fields.tab_content_3:
A 2:10 am lockout waits on Kwabena first

Night shift at Tumbridge Cold Storage runs from 10 pm to 6 am. Philippa Lusk is locked out of her scanner sign-in at 2:10 am and files from the break-room kiosk. Requests filed in those hours go to shift supervisor Kwabena Hesketh, who confirms she is on shift. On-call tech Dashiell Brannagh then gets it by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who keeps getting locked out, by name and count

Fenmarch Hotels runs one IT team for 3 properties. Its October dashboard shows 58 reset requests: 23 for email, 19 for the front desk, 10 for payroll, and 6 for bookings. Four staff filed 14 of the 58 requests, each with 3 or more in 30 days. IT director Yevgenia Tolliver books the four a self-service setup session.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Password Reset Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a password reset form that confirms who is asking before IT resets any account.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide how IT confirms who is asking
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give possible misuse its own path
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every system staff sign in to, such as email, payroll, the VPN, and a shared front desk login. Each one becomes a choice on the form. Next to each, write the name of the person who can reset it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for what IT needs to find the person and the account they lost. Add no field for the old password or a new one, so nobody can type one into a request by mistake.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick one check the tech runs before any reset. A call to the number in the staff directory works when everyone has a desk phone or a work mobile. Never call back a number the requester supplies, since whoever filed the request chose it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a choice for possible misuse to the list of what happened. Choose who hears about those requests, such as a security lead or the owner. Put them ahead of forgotten passwords in the queue.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the account list, the check, and the routing into one prompt. Emergent builds the form and the table of requests behind it. To change a field or a route later, say what you want in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan for lockouts when IT is off
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what happens to a request filed outside IT hours. A supervisor on site can confirm the person is working that shift before the on-call tech gets it. Write the exact hours into the prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: File a fake lockout from a phone and from a shared computer. Check that each request reaches the right person, that the tech can tick Verified only after the call, and that an Urgent request sits at the top of the queue.

faq_plan.q: What is a password reset form?
faq_plan.a: A password reset form is the request a locked-out employee sends to IT to get back into one named account. It records who is asking, which account is locked, and what happened, and it never asks for the password itself. IT checks the person's identity before anyone resets the account.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a password reset form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in one prompt in Emergent's AI form builder: the accounts people sign in to, who resets each one, and how IT confirms the caller. For example: "Build a password reset form for my 24-hour call center that emails each request to my IT lead." Emergent builds the form and its database from that sentence. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a password reset form template ask for?
faq_plan.a: Five fields cover it: the person's name and work email, their employee ID, the account that is locked, and a short list of what happened, such as a forgotten password or a lockout after failed tries. A password reset form template should hold no field for a password, old or new. Replace the sample account list with the systems people sign in to before you share it.

faq_plan.q: Should a password reset form also collect other requests?
faq_plan.hint: How to use password reset form in django?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep the form to lost access. Then every request in the queue is one IT can verify and close in a single call. A request for a new report or a change to an internal tool belongs on a feature request form, where whoever owns that tool can weigh it against other work.

faq_plan.q: Should a password reset form make staff change passwords on a schedule?
faq_plan.a: No. NIST's digital identity guidelines say verifiers and CSPs shall not require subscribers to change passwords periodically. The same section says verifiers shall force a change if there is evidence that the authenticator has been compromised. A request flagged as possible misuse is the case for a forced change, not the calendar.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve the requests a password reset form collects?
faq_plan.a: The person who runs that account should approve it. Email resets go to the help desk, and payroll resets go to whoever controls payroll access. Name a backup for each. A request filed during a vacation then still has an owner. In a form built on Emergent, the app sends each request to its approver by email or Slack.

faq_plan.q: How is a password reset form different from a general help desk ticket?
faq_plan.a: A password reset form handles one job: getting a locked-out person back into an account after IT confirms who they are. A general help desk ticket covers everything else, from a broken printer to a software install. Send those through an IT request form. Lockouts then never wait behind a printer.

faq_plan.q: How do you verify the person behind a password reset form request?
faq_plan.a: Call them back at a number you already hold, from the staff directory or HR records. For remote staff with no desk line, use the work mobile on file, or have their manager confirm them on a video call. Write who did the check, and how, on the request before the reset.

faq_plan.q: Who should be able to see what a password reset form collects?
faq_plan.a: Only the staff who work the reset queue. In an app built on Emergent, the requests live in a database you own, and that table shows who was locked out of which account and when. Keep closed requests for your monthly count instead of deleting them.

faq_plan.q: What should a password reset form record when a request is closed?
faq_plan.a: Record the time it closed, the tech's name, and the check they ran. If the lockout came from a lost or broken work phone, point the employee to the equipment request form for a replacement. Then watch the monthly count for anyone who files again within a few weeks.

plan.angle: Results for this query are login-screen tutorials and end-user help articles on recovering one account. This page treats the password reset form as the request a locked-out employee sends to IT: five fields (name, work email, employee ID, the account, what happened), no field for any password, a callback to the number on file before the reset, an urgent path when someone else may have used the account, a supervisor check on night shifts and a monthly count of resets by account. General IT tickets, access grants and device requests belong to sibling pages, which the FAQ links instead of answering. No security certification claims; the NIST lines are quoted inside their own scope.
